BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect.

The 29-year-old suspect Daniel Bowen Payne was held in Schuyler County Jail on a $1 million bond. Prosecutors approved pursuing one count of attempted first-degree murder of a police officer. Daniel's attorney requested a court change due to potential local bias and sought to suppress evidence, claiming he was unlawfully detained after fleeing due to an officer drawing a weapon. He was sentenced to 28 and a half years in prison, with court costs waived for time served. Under Illinois truth in sentencing laws, he must serve at least 85% of his sentence, about 24 years and three months, making him eligible for release in December 2048 at nearly 55 years old.
